source.publication: Joseph H. Silverman, The Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves, second edition, Springer2009
source.locator: VI Corollary5.1.1 and Proposition5.2, printed173–174; Proposition5.4(a), printed175

rows.available: For every elliptic curve over C, integration of an invariant differential identifies its complex Lie group with C/Lambda for its full rank-two period lattice. The torsion subgroup is (1/m)Lambda/Lambda.
rows.needed: For the actual real curve and a real invariant differential, obtain the full period lattice and finite torsion identifications before proving integral conjugation splitting.
rows.derivation: Complex conjugation of paths conjugates the integral of the real differential. This proves equivariance; the trivial action on E[2] then forces (J-1)Lambda subset2Lambda and gives integral projectors. Neither equivariance nor integral splitting is attributed to a rational eigenbasis alone.
rows.boundary: General complex uniformization is used; no CM hypothesis or CM-specific model is imported.

rows.available: Finite real Tate cup duality for E[2^n] is perfect after Weil self-duality.
rows.needed: Once the actual minus-line Kummer subgroup is computed and shown isotropic, order2 in the order4 cohomology group gives its exact annihilator.
rows.boundary: The finite duality theorem supplies perfection only. The actual lattice and Kummer subgroup are constructed in preceding proof lines.
